findings.title: Published audit run uses two conflicting finding-ID schemes in the same report
evidence: docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261007-1731-main-4ecee97/lens_focused_security_supply_chain_ci.md:7-13 - summary table uses SUPPLY-P1-001, SUPPLY-P2-001, SUPPLY-P2-002, DATA-P2-001, SAFE-P2-001, CI-P3-001, GOV-P3-001
docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261007-1731-main-4ecee97/lens_focused_security_supply_chain_ci.md:71 - heading 'SUPPLY-P2-002 - nvfancontrol' but the table/JSON id for the same finding is SUPPLY-P2-001

docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261007-1731-main-4ecee97/lens_focused_security_supply_chain_ci.md:79,87,97,108,115 - body headings use SUPPLY-P2-003, DATA-P2-004, SAFE-P2-005, CI-P3-006, GOV-P3-007 (ordinal scheme) while findings.json uses SUPPLY-P2-002, DATA-P2-001, SAFE-P2-001, CI-P3-001, GOV-P3-001 (per-area scheme)
docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261007-1731-main-4ecee97/findings.json:22,41,59,77,95,113,130 - machine-readable ids confirm the per-area (-001) scheme
docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261007-1731-main-4ecee97/follow_up_register.md:5-11 - register rows use the per-area ids, so a reader following a body heading lands on the wrong row
findings.impact: The single human-readable report and the machine-readable aggregate disagree on finding identity for every finding after the first. Remediation agents and operators cross-referencing the narrative to findings.json/registers will map fixes to the wrong finding, breaking traceability that the orchestration contract requires.
findings.recommendation: Adopt one ID scheme (the per-area AREA-SEVERITY-NNN form used in findings.json) and regenerate every section heading, the summary table, and the registers from findings.json so all artifacts share identical IDs; add a check that headings and JSON ids match.

findings.title: risk_register.md is a byte-for-byte copy of follow_up_register.md, so the run has no risk aggregation
evidence: docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261007-1731-main-4ecee97/risk_register.md:1 - title is 'Follow-up register' (not a risk register)
git diff --no-index docs/audits/.../risk_register.md docs/audits/.../follow_up_register.md exits 0 (no differences) - the two files are identical
docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261007-1731-main-4ecee97/INDEX.md:12 - presents 'risk_register.md / follow_up_register.md' as if they were distinct 'Findings register' artifacts
findings.impact: The orchestrator scope explicitly requires defining aggregation categories for a final risk register. Here the risk register carries no risk fields (no likelihood, impact, or category), so the run cannot roll findings into a risk view; the duplicate also inflates the apparent artifact set.
findings.recommendation: Replace risk_register.md with a genuine aggregation (category, severity, likelihood, impact, evidence, mitigation) derived from findings.json, and keep follow_up_register.md as the owner/target/status tracker so the two have distinct purposes.

findings.title: Run INDEX and audit_manifest.json omit the deterministic lens artifacts
evidence: docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261007-1731-main-4ecee97/INDEX.md:7-15 - file table lists neither lens_deterministic.md nor deterministic-findings.json
git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD -- docs/audits/ - both lens_deterministic.md and deterministic-findings.json are tracked in the run folder
docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261007-1731-main-4ecee97/deterministic-findings.json:20 - findings reference report 'lens_deterministic.md', proving the lens is part of the run
findings.impact: The run manifest and INDEX are the operator handoff map. Omitting two produced reports means a reader reproducing the run cannot tell that a deterministic lens ran or find its output, and no artifact states which reports are intentionally excluded.
findings.recommendation: List lens_deterministic.md and deterministic-findings.json in both INDEX.md and audit_manifest.json scope.reports; if any artifact is intentionally excluded from the aggregate, record it explicitly as excluded.

findings.title: Deterministic finding DET-P3-002 is dropped from the aggregate with no exclusion record
evidence: docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261007-1731-main-4ecee97/deterministic-findings.json:14-34 - deterministic lens emitted two findings: DET-P3-001 (no CI) and DET-P3-002 (.gitattributes missing)
docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261007-1731-main-4ecee97/findings.json:5-18 - aggregate counts total 7 with byArea SUPPLY/DATA/SAFE/CI/GOV; no DET area and no DET-P3-002 anywhere
docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261007-1731-main-4ecee97/findings.json:125 - only DET-P3-001 is carried over (as CI-P3-001 deterministic_ref)
findings.impact: The aggregate silently loses one machine-generated finding. Aggregates must state excluded items explicitly, otherwise a later reproduction or score sees a different finding count than the run actually produced.
findings.recommendation: Either merge DET-P3-002 into the aggregate or list it under an explicit 'excluded / superseded' note in findings.json and INDEX.md, and record the merge rule used.

findings.title: Published run was never reconciled after later commits fixed two of its findings
evidence: docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261007-1731-main-4ecee97/findings.json:113-128 - CI-P3-001 'No CI, dependency automation, or secret scanning' status is 'open'
git log --oneline --diff-filter=A -- .github/workflows/build-app.yml -> 14b0b0e3 'feat(app): standalone GUI/TUI/agent bundles via PyInstaller + CI' added the workflows
git log --oneline --diff-filter=A -- .gitattributes -> 71772649 'fix(runners,ui,live,packaging): close the audit findings' added the line-ending policy (resolves DET-P3-002)
docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261007-1731-main-4ecee97/follow_up_register.md:10-11 - CI-P3-001 and GOV-P3-001 remain 'open' with no reconciliation note
findings.impact: The check-in state shows findings as open that the repository has since addressed, with no reconciliation artifact. An operator reading the register cannot distinguish resolved from outstanding work, which is exactly what the post-audit reconciliation step exists to prevent.
findings.recommendation: Add a reconciliation pass that updates each finding's status to verified-fixed (with the fixing commit as artifact) or still-open, and record the reconciliation date/commit in INDEX.md.

# Audit Orchestrator

## Audit Metadata

The only orchestration artifact set inside the target is the one published run under `docs/audits/`.

## Scope

Reviewed the repository's audit-orchestration surface: repository type / monorepo boundaries, the app/service/package map, the published audit run under `docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261007-1731-main-4ecee97/`, run naming, report inventory, risk aggregation, finding-ID scheme, do-not-touch rules, and operator handoff. Not reviewed: the benchmark phases, the control plane, the live-USB build, and CI workflow internals (owned by other domains). The target working tree had two pre-existing uncommitted modifications (`server/benchd.py`, `server/import_results.py`) that were not touched.

## Evidence Reviewed

- `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `VERSION`, `.gitattributes`
- `docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261007-1731-main-4ecee97/` — all 12 tracked files
- git history for the audit run, `.github/`, and `.gitattributes`

## Verification Performed

## Executive Summary

`bench-test` is a **single-package workstation toolkit** (not a SaaS, not a monorepo): a flat layout of `bench/`, `server/`, `live/`, `packaging/`, `tests/`, `docs/`, `examples/`, `results/`, documented in `README.md:326-336` and `AGENTS.md:48-60`. Nothing here implements the audit-orchestration pipeline itself — that pipeline (scaffolding, publishing, digests) is the *repo-deep-dive* pack's job. What the target *does* contain is one published audit run serving as the worked example of the run contract, and that run is internally inconsistent.

Strengths: run folder naming follows the pack convention (`YYYYMMDD-HHMM-{branch}-{shortsha}` → `20261007-1731-main-4ecee97`); a machine-readable `audit_manifest.json` with `outputRoot`, prompt list, and commit binding exists; the report has a `Verification Performed` section that distinguishes lab-unavailable (`MODE=local`) and records it honestly; the repo declares do-not-touch rules (`AGENTS.md:279-285`).

Risks: the published run uses **two conflicting finding-ID schemes**, its `risk_register.md` is a **verbatim duplicate** of the follow-up register, the manifest/INDEX **omit two produced reports**, one deterministic finding is **silently dropped** from the aggregate, and the register is **never reconciled** after later commits fixed two findings. ## Findings

### Finding ID: ORCH-P2-001 - Published audit run uses two conflicting finding-ID schemes

- Area: ORCH (finding ID scheme)

- What is happening: the narrative and the machine-readable aggregate disagree on the ID of every finding after the first.
- Why it matters: cross-referencing a body heading to `findings.json`/the register resolves to a different finding.
- Recommended fix: regenerate all headings from `findings.json` and add a consistency check.
